previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide and cyclophosphamide, was admitted with neck pain present for three days, likely musculoskeletal in origin. An MRI of the cervical spine showed slightly worsened spinal stenosis at C3-C4 without cord compression or acute myeloma involvement. During the admission, he developed a fever and was found to have right lower lobe pneumonia on chest imaging, which was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral levofloxacin. He received one unit of PRBCs for symptomatic anemia and was managed for chronic kidney disease and subtherapeutic INR, with warfarin held due to recent nosebleed. His Revlimid was paused due to infection and cytopenias. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans to follow up with oncology and spine surgery. Blood cultures remained negative at discharge.
problems: Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with multiple medical problems, notably 
multiple myeloma, COPD, CAD, a-fib and spinal stenosis, who had 
a recent admission for neck pain and pneumonia, being admitted 
for toe pain and erythema.
  
#  Toe erythema: His first toe on the right foot had an 
ulcer/pre-ulcer at the very tip of the toe, likely from stubbing 
it, with surrounding erythema to the midfoot. He denied any 
pain, fevers, or drainage from the toe. Because of his history 
of gangrene on the second digit, and his recent hospitalization, 
he was admitted for IV antibiotics. He was treated with 1 gram 
IV vancomycin and the toe improved. He had an X-ray of the foot 
which was negative for osteo on wet-read, and he was seen by 
podiatry. They debrided the wound and felt that it looked well. 
He will have follow-up on ___ in the outpatient 
___ clinic.

#  Acute on chronic renal failure: Likely secondary to 
dehydration as his creatinine increased from 1.9 to 2.4 from 
discharge. Also, his CBC appeared to be hemoconcentrated based 
on his admission labs. He was hydrated with 2L of NS and his 
creatinine improved to 2. He will have his labs checked on 
___ at follow-up. 

#  Anemia: After hydration, Mr. ___ HCT was 21. He was 
transfused one unit of PRBCs and his HCT responded appropriately 
to 25.5. He will have follow-up ___ and have his labs 
checked.

#  Pneumonia: He was diagnosed during his last admission and was 
discharged on levofloxacin. He has been afebrile, still has a 
cough, though it is improved. He was initially continued on the 
levofloxacin, however, he became sleepy with some clonic 
movements of his upper and lower extremities (clonic jerks that 
were infrequent). He had become encephalopathic during his past 
admission on levofloxacin, so we changed his antibiotics to 
cefpodoxime BID and azithromycin daily.

#  Multiple myeloma: His CBC was depressed on admission after 
hydration. He is recieving treatment as an outpatient.

#  Chronic pain: He has spinal stenosis, and is on a home 
regimen of gabapentin, oxycontin, and oxycodone. We continued 
his home meds renally dosed.

# COPD: Stable. We continued prn nebs, and switched to Advair 
from Symbicort in hospital because Symbicort was not on 
formulary.

# Transfer of care: Mr. ___ had a PICC placed and was 
discharged with home infusion for vancomycin for 5 days. He will 
be seen on ___ in ___ ___. At discharge, his foot 
x-ray final report was pending.
